goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same mistake: end is computed from slotStartTime when it should use slotEndTime.

goldens.comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the same bug: === compares dayjs objects by reference, so the check is always false.

candidates: Line 142 computes end using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, making end identical to start, so the working hours boundary check never catches slots that start within working hours but extend past the end

Line 114 uses === to compare two distinct dayjs objects by reference, which is always false in JavaScript, breaking detection of 'day off' date overrides where start equals end and allowing slots to be booked on days the organizer marked as unavailable

checkIfIsAvailable() returns true immediately when a date override exists for the slot day, skipping the busy-time overlap checks, which can allow bookings that overlap existing busy events on days with overrides (double-booking)

When multiple date override ranges exist on the same date, checkIfIsAvailable() rejects a slot if it falls outside any one range, effectively requiring the slot to be inside all ranges, making valid slots unavailable when a user has multiple override ranges on the same day
